testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave with the other hand.
Press hard on the brakes.
Do not use the brakes.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using brakes during a tire failure can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking unless you must to avoid a crash. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Then brake gently, move off the road, and stop.

questions.question: How do states ensure people have only one driver's license?

options.text: You must sign a form.
States share driver information in a computer database.
They search your wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: States share driver information in a computer database.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have more than one driver's license. All states use a shared computer database to check driver information. This prevents people from getting multiple licenses.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The tires grip the road better.
The vehicle is easier to control.
The vehicle becomes heavier.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road and slide on a layer of water instead.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Pull the air brake lever.
Move the brake lever forward.
Press down on the brake pedal.
Pull up on the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down on the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?

options.text: Exposure to sunlight.
Exposure to moisture.
Using the brakes too much.
Not using the brakes enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes too much.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes too much causes them to overheat and work less well. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what is likely to happen?

options.text: It will probably stay green when you reach it.
It is probably broken.
It will likely change to yellow soon.
It will skip yellow and go straight to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will likely change to yellow soon.
questions.explanation: If a light has been green for a long time, it will probably turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When checking brakes, a slack adjuster should move how much from where it connects to the push rod?

options.text: At least three inches
More than two inches
Up to five inches
No more than one inch

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than one inch
questions.explanation: Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than one inch from the push rod. If it moves more than one inch, it is out of adjustment and needs to be fixed.

questions.question: Where can retreaded tires be used on a bus?

options.text: Anywhere on the bus.
On the front wheels.
On the rear wheels.
Retreaded tires cannot be used on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They can only be used on the rear wheels.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity.
They usually have high centers of gravity.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.
They cannot be driven on interstates.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need careful driving. The material inside can shift during transport, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: What does it mean if the ABS warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: The ABS is working properly.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. If the light comes on, something is wrong with the system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: When should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped on a level surface.
When your vehicle is stopped on a slight incline.
When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When your vehicle's other braking systems are working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are very hot from driving downhill or if they are wet in freezing weather. Using the parking brake on hot brakes can damage them. Using brakes when they are wet and frozen can cause them to ice up and lock the vehicle.

questions.question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as possible.
Release the steering wheel.
Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Stop on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly if a tire fails. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once it has slowed down significantly, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: Looking far ahead when driving is:

options.text: Discouraged because what is ahead is less important than where you are now.
Encouraged so you can see hazards early and have time to react.
Not allowed.
Only encouraged when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged so you can see hazards early and have time to react.
questions.explanation: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This helps you spot hazards early so you have time to respond safely.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use curved convex mirrors. They let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: Where should you place cargo that does not fill the entire trailer?

options.text: At the front of the trailer.
At the rear of the trailer.
In the middle of the trailer.
Anywhere in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Balance the cargo so weight is even on the front and rear axles. Unbalanced cargo can damage your vehicle and make it harder to control.

questions.question: Which statement about turn signals is NOT correct?

options.text: Signal early.
Signal continuously.
Turn off your signal when your turn or lane change is complete.
Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby. Signal early and keep it on during the entire turn or lane change. Turn it off when you are done.

questions.question: Friction in a brake drum happens when brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against each other.
Separate from the axle.
Push against the inside of the drum.
Create excess heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction forms when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To keep cargo from moving during transport.
To keep cargo from being loaded too high.
To keep cargo from being unloaded too quickly.
To make cargo harder to unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from sliding during transport.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Stay in one lane.
Have a plan for emergencies.
Stay in the left lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a plan for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Scan the road for potential hazards. Plan how you will respond if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road would make the driver carsick.
Having part of your vehicle in the mirror gives you a point of reference.
It is illegal to show only the road in the mirrors.
You need to see reflections of vehicles on the trailer in the mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Having part of your vehicle in the mirror gives you a point of reference.
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This helps you judge how close other vehicles and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on gear use. What should you NOT do?

options.text: Grind or clash gears.
Pick a gear that doesn't rev the engine too much.
Shift gears while going through an intersection.
Shift gears while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears while turning.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on gear use. Choose a gear that doesn't rev or strain the engine. Avoid grinding gears, clashing gears, and shifting during turns or intersections.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks.
Activates the emergency brakes if there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first main storage tank. It prevents air from escaping the brake system if the air compressor leaks.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving normally.
Safely exit the road and park as soon as possible.
Stop immediately where you are.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the road and park as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, safely leave the road and park right away. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
After you finish driving.
Mirrors don't need to be adjusted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver acts aggressively toward you?

options.text: Make eye contact with them.
Block their way on the road.
Don't react to their angry gestures.
Try to talk to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't react to their angry gestures.
questions.explanation: If another driver acts aggressively, the best thing to do is get out of their way. Don't make eye contact, don't speed up to challenge them, and don't react to angry gestures.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
To make sure the vehicle gets inspected regularly.
To hold drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
To plan the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets the driver tell the motor carrier about issues that could affect safe driving. Drivers should fill out this report after each day of driving and note any safety issues or problems that could cause a breakdown.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to move out of your way.
Drive on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy need special permits. These vehicles can usually only be driven at certain times.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.
The speed of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What can happen if cargo is not loaded properly?

options.text: It might look bad to other drivers.
It could injure the driver if you stop suddenly.
It makes it easier to stop.
It helps with safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could injure the driver if you stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and secured correctly so it doesn't fall or shift. During a sudden stop, improperly loaded cargo could hurt or kill the driver.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Set the parking brake.
Apply the air brakes.
Don't apply any brake.
Unhook the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Ability to focus
Daydreaming
Yawning repeatedly
Drifting from your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Fatigue is dangerous while driving. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in a vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not focus on the road and could make unsafe moves. Children may not watch for traffic and could run into the road. Be careful near road workers to keep them safe. A person waiting for a bus on a bench is not a traffic concern.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a serious traffic violation?

options.text: Improper lane usage.
Having multiple licenses.
Using a cell phone.
Not stopping behind the stop line at a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not stopping behind the stop line at a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include speeding too fast, reckless driving, driving a commercial vehicle without a valid license, following too closely, and improper lane usage. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your license.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle?

options.text: 10 psi in one minute
8 psi in one minute
6 psi in one minute
4 psi in one minute

questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: Know the safe maximum air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should lose no more than 6 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.

options.text: White ice
Black ice
Green ice
Blue ice

questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, which makes the road look like it is just wet.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob
Start the vehicle
Tap the accelerator twice

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob
Use the accelerator
Tap the accelerator twice

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, a yellow diamond-shaped knob controls the parking brakes. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: When going down a long hill, you should brake by:

options.text: Only using the brakes
Using the brakes mostly and downshifting occasionally
Downshifting first, then using brakes
Never using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using brakes
questions.explanation: On a downhill grade, use your engine's braking power as your main way to slow down. Use the brakes only if you need extra slowing or stopping for traffic or road conditions.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle
1,000 feet of your vehicle
Your view of the road ahead
One minute of hitting the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead on the road. Slow down when visibility is reduced.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used carefully because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire
Other drivers may not see the flares
Flares are expensive
Other drivers may get confused

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire
questions.explanation: After an accident, spilled fuel combined with flares can start a fire. Use flares carefully to avoid this danger.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Look at the tires.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop a short distance later?

options.text: To check that the lug nuts are tight.
To check that the tire tread is good.
To make sure the correct tire was changed.
To see if rocks are stuck in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How should cargo be secured on flatbed trailers?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during the trip.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does it mean if other vehicles are not creating spray?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The pavement is dry.
The spray is stuck under the vehicle.
The tires have absorbed all the moisture.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles are not creating spray, ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: Is a pre-trip vehicle inspection required?

options.text: No, not if you use the vehicle regularly.
No, not for trips under 100 miles.
No, only a mechanic needs to do it.
Yes, it is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required by law.
questions.explanation: Drivers are required by state and federal law to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: What happens when brakes fade while driving down a steep grade?

options.text: They become quieter.
They become less effective.
They work better than usual.
They work differently from front to back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: When you use your brakes too much on a steep downgrade, they overheat and become less effective. Use engine braking instead to avoid overheating your brakes on steep hills.

questions.question: When should you check cargo to make sure it is secure?

options.text: Only before the trip starts.
Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
Only by loading personnel.
Only when you arrive at the destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting your trip and again after the first 50 miles. Also check it every three hours or 150 miles after that. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured the entire trip.

questions.question: Is it good practice to look far ahead while driving?

options.text: No, because you cannot do anything about problems far away.
Yes, it helps you spot hazards early.
No, it is not allowed.
Yes, only if you are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to identify hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: After a trailer starts to turn while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turn the steering wheel farther in the same direction.
Use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only accept incoming calls.
Text instead of calling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid cell phone distractions, turn your phone off before you start driving and leave it off until you reach your destination.
